name: Sahitya Readiness Scan for PHP
author: sahitya10

sections.description:
Your host emailed you: “We’re upgrading your site to PHP 8.x.” Will your site still work?

Sahitya Readiness Scan is a PHP compatibility checker for WordPress. It reads the code of every plugin and theme on your site and tells you, in plain English:

  • A readiness score, for example “92% ready for PHP 8.4”.
  • A clear verdict for each plugin and theme: “No issues found”, “Likely compatible” (warnings only), or “Issues found” (will likely break).
  • What to do next, without technical jargon. The technical details are still there if you or your developer want them.
  • Does updating fix it? For plugins from WordPress.org, it checks the newest version for you: “Updating 3.1 → 3.24 fixes this”, or “The latest version still has issues”.
  • Step-by-step guides for changing the PHP version at SiteGround, Hostinger, Bluehost, GoDaddy, Kinsta, WP Engine and any cPanel host.

Why now

PHP 8.1 stopped getting security fixes at the end of 2025, and PHP 8.2 stops on 31 December 2026. Most hosts move sites to a newer version soon after. Run a scan before your host does it for you, so you know which plugins to update first.

Built for cheap hosting

The scan runs in small steps of a few seconds each, so it never times out, even on hosting with a 30-second limit. You can pause it, or close the page: it carries on in the background and picks up where it left off.

Scan only

This plugin never changes, updates or deletes your plugins or themes. It only reads their files.

What gets checked

  • All plugins, active and inactive
  • Must-use plugins
  • Your active theme and its parent theme
  • Target versions PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5

The checks come from the open-source PHPCompatibility rules (PHPCompatibilityWP), running inside WordPress. No exec() or command line needed.

Not affiliated with PHP

Sahitya Readiness Scan is an independent plugin. It is not made, endorsed or supported by the PHP project or the PHP Group. “PHP” is used only to say which language versions it checks.

Source code and bundled libraries

The scanning rules come from PHP_CodeSniffer and PHPCompatibility, which are bundled in the vendor-prefixed folder. They are needed at runtime: they are the scanner itself, not development tools. They are renamed into their own namespace (PHPUC\Vendor\) so they never clash with other plugins that ship the same libraries. composer.json, composer.lock and scoper.inc.php show exactly which versions are bundled and how they are built.

Important

This is a static scan: it reads the code without running it. It can’t catch every runtime problem. Always back up your site and, if you can, test on a staging copy before switching PHP.

External services

This plugin connects to the official WordPress.org plugin directory, and nothing else.

  • What and why: for plugins where the scan found problems, it asks the WordPress.org Plugins API (api.wordpress.org) for the latest version of that plugin. If a newer version exists, it downloads that version’s ZIP file from downloads.wordpress.org to a temporary folder, scans it, and deletes it. This is how it can tell you whether updating fixes the problem.
  • What is sent: the same as WordPress itself sends when it checks for plugin updates: the plugin’s WordPress.org name (slug), plus your WordPress version and site address in the standard WordPress request header. No other data is sent. There is no tracking and no analytics.
  • When: only after a scan you started, and only for plugins with issues or warnings. Results are cached for 7 days.
  • How to turn it off: Tools → Readiness Scan → Settings → untick “Check newer versions”.
  • WordPress.org terms and privacy policy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. In your dashboard go to Plugins → Add New, search for “Sahitya Readiness Scan for PHP”, then Install and Activate.
  2. Go to Tools → Readiness Scan.
  3. Pick the PHP version your host is moving you to (or keep “Automatic”) and click Start scan.
sections.faq:
Which PHP version should I pick?

The one your host is moving you to. If you don’t know, keep “Automatic”: it checks the next version up from the one your site runs now. You can scan again for another version at any time.

My site runs PHP 7.4 or 8.0. Can I use it?

Yes. The plugin itself runs on PHP 7.4 and newer. It checks your code against PHP 8.2 or later, which is where your host will most likely move you.

Does this guarantee my site won’t break?

No. No tool can promise that. This plugin reads the code without running it, so it finds most problems but not all of them. Use it to find the plugins that need attention, then back up your site and test on staging before you switch.

Will it slow down my site?

No. It only works while a scan is running, in short steps. Visitors don’t notice. When a scan is finished it does nothing.

Will it change or update my plugins?

No. It never changes, updates or deletes anything. Even the “does updating fix it?” check only downloads a temporary copy, scans it, and deletes it. You decide whether to update.

What does “Likely compatible” mean?

The plugin uses something PHP has marked as old (deprecated). It should keep working, but it may write warnings to your error log. Updating the plugin usually fixes it.

A plugin shows “Issues found”. What now?

  1. Look at the line under it: if updating fixes it, update the plugin before you switch PHP.
  2. If the latest version still has issues, contact the plugin’s developer or look for an alternative plugin.
  3. Click “Show details” to see the exact files and lines, for you or your developer.

What does “Couldn’t check” mean?

A file was very large, or needed more time or memory than your server allows, so it was skipped. These are usually generated data files, not code that breaks. If it worries you, ask the plugin’s developer.

My plugin isn’t from WordPress.org. Can it still be checked?

Yes, the installed version is scanned like any other. Only the “does updating fix it?” check needs WordPress.org, so for premium plugins ask the developer whether the latest version supports your PHP version.

Does it send my data anywhere?

Only the requests to WordPress.org described under “External services” above, and you can turn those off. There is no tracking.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

It removes everything it stored: its database tables, settings, cached results and temporary files.
sections.changelog:
0.7.0

  • New: after a scan finishes, a small box asks if you’d like to leave a review. It shows until you click “Leave a review” or “No thanks”, then never again.
  • Better plugin directory description, tags and FAQ.

0.6.0

  • New name: Sahitya Readiness Scan for PHP (slug: sahitya-readiness-scan).

0.5.0

  • Fixed: database tables are now created correctly on MySQL servers in strict mode.
  • The scan screen explains the problem if the database tables can’t be created.

0.4.1

  • Fixed: database queries now all use prepared statements (Plugin Check warnings).

0.4.0

  • New: “Does updating fix it?” check for plugins from WordPress.org (can be turned off in Settings).
  • Changed: internal prefix renamed to phpuc.

0.3.0

  • New: readiness score, plain-English results, filters, search, Re-scan button, host upgrade guides.

0.2.0

  • New: chunked background scan that never times out, with pause, resume and cancel.

0.1.0

  • First version: scanning engine and test fixtures.
